scope_basis: Data and artificial intelligence innovation centre.
title: Data Innovation Centre for Artificial Intelligence
description: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) in Africa faces several challenges that need to be overcome for its efficient adoption and implementation in support of sustainable development. For example, studies indicate many shortcomings in terms of data as well as insufficient skills and AI innovations in key sectors such as agriculture, health, environment and transport. The Data Innovation Centre for AI seeks to address these shortcomings within Senegal and beyond through a multidisciplinary collaboration with practitioners in data, AI, agriculture, health and the environment. This project will support strengthening skills in data and AI and the production and sharing of reliable, high-quality data with decision-makers in priority sectors. It will also foster the development of inclusive and responsible AI resources and innovations that benefit communities. Similarly, the project will take up the challenge of inclusion through a mechanism to integrate more women as well as people from disadvantaged groups (such as people living with disabilities) into the data and AI ecosystem. This project is a part of the Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) program, a five-year partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to support policy, innovations and expanded leadership to spur safe and responsible AI development and use in Africa. The vision of the new partnership is to support an inclusive, responsible AI ecosystem that improves quality of life for all in Africa and beyond.

scope_basis: Living lab on artificial intelligence policy and systems in Senegal.

description: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and its potential to achieve sustainable development goals and boost economic growth means that mastering it is increasingly crucial for every country to ensure its technological, economic, social and political sovereignty. To this end, an AI Continental White Paper and Roadmap, a strategic blueprint leading to the development of the African Union Continental AI Strategy, was recently launched. Several African countries, including Senegal, have also published national AI strategies. The Government of Senegal has also published a national data strategy and seeks to pool the two strategies in their implementation. This project supports the AI Living Labs for Innovative and Viable Ethical Policies and Systems (AI Living Lab), based in Dakar, Senegal, which is building an AI innovation ecosystem around three major axes: (i) a collaborative technological platform integrating powerful AI algorithms and a large database; (ii) cutting-edge and inclusive scientific work on responsible AI, inter- and multi-disciplinary, focused on achieving sustainable development goals; and (iii) popularization and promotion of AI, particularly with regard to young people, decision-makers and socio-economic stakeholders. This project is a part of the AI4D program, a five-year partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to support policy, innovations and expanded leadership to spur safe and responsible AI development and use in Africa. The vision of the new partnership is to support an inclusive, responsible AI ecosystem that improves quality of life for all in Africa and beyond.

scope_basis: Improves management and open sharing of research data.
title: Strengthening the management and sharing of research data
description: Governments, research funders, scholarly publishers, and academic organizations are increasingly advocating for greater openness to research data to catalyze innovation and collaboration and to uphold research integrity by allowing others to query or build on research findings. While these rationales are compelling, the management, curation, and archiving of research data in open repositories is not established practice in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. This project seeks to strengthen the management and sharing of research data generated through IDRC-funded research projects. The project will invite researchers funded by IDRC to participate in a peer-learning process that will result in their data being archived in appropriate data repositories. This will involve the development of data management plans, papers describing their data, and the curation of datasets. The process will be guided by international advisors who will help researchers understand the administrative process, ethical considerations, and data curation techniques that support the archiving of research data in open repositories. As researcher practices and infrastructures vary across regions, the project will convene workshops in Africa, Asia, and South America to exchange experiences in the management and sharing of research data in each region. Insights from peer exchanges and guidance provided by the international advisors will be used by researchers to publish their data papers and archive their data. IDRC staff will contribute to and learn from these peer-learning processes to improve the guidance the Centre provides to grantees in support of its Open Data Statement of Principles.

title: Project for the Establishment of ISEP (Institut Supérieur d'Enseignement Professionnel) in Dakar, Senegal
description: KOICA grant ($9.4M, 2015-2021) to establish the ISEP technical college at Diamniadio, Senegal with ICT and automotive engineering departments. Provides vocational ICT education aligned with industry needs. Includes ICT lab equipment, faculty training, and curriculum development.
